key_insight: Program-as-Weights turns a natural-language function specification into a compact neural artifact, so fuzzy tasks can run locally and repeatedly instead of relying on per-query LLM calls.
engineering_relevance: This is useful for building low-latency, offline, and cost-efficient systems for messy real-world tasks like log alerts, JSON repair, and intent-based ranking.
method: Train a 4B compiler on FuzzyBench to map specifications into parameter-efficient adapters.
Execute the resulting adapters with a frozen 0.6B Qwen3 interpreter.
Use one-time compilation per function definition, then reuse the artifact for cheap subsequent calls.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a released 10M-example FuzzyBench dataset and that a 0.6B Qwen3 interpreter with PAW matches direct prompting of Qwen3-32B while using about one-fiftieth of the inference memory and reaching 30 tokens/s on a MacBook M3.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the compiler-generated adapter, so robustness and generalization across unseen fuzzy functions may be an implementation risk.
paper_title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
